diagnosis: Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) with minimal differentiation
legend: Immunophenotype of blasts by flow cytometry. Blasts (in red) express CD34, CD13, KIT (CD117), and CD7, but lack cCD3 and myeloperoxidase. Populations in blue represent normal lymphocytes, monocytes, and granulocytes.

diagnosis: Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) with minimal differentiation
legend: Cytomorphology of blasts. A Giemsa-stained smear showing blasts lacking morphological evidence of myeloid differentiation. These are medium-sized to large, with dispersed nuclear chromatin and round or slightly indented nuclei. The cytoplasm lacks granules or Auer rods and has a variable degree of basophilia. B Myeloperoxidase-stained smear showing blasts lacking expression of myeloperoxidase. The cell with positive myeloperoxidase staining is an eosinophil (internal control).
